title: LeMon: Automating Portrait Generation for Zero-Shot Story Visualization with Multi-Character Interactions

problem.claim: Automated multi-character zero-shot story visualization must create distinctive yet compatible character portraits without manual intervention.

gap.claim: Existing approaches require inefficient manual collection of external images for initial character portraits and can produce low-quality visualizations during multi-character interactions.

contributions.claim: LeMon is an LLM-enhanced multi-character zero-shot visualization framework that automates character portrait initialization and supports iterative refinement using story semantics.
The framework matches story characters with external movie characters and uses the matched resources as in-context learning samples to initialize portraits.
A graph-based Text2Image diffusion model constructs a character interaction graph and iteratively refines portraits to increase character distinctness while reducing incompatibility.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LeMon outperforms existing zero-shot story visualization approaches on stories of various types involving multiple interacting characters.

narrative_sequence.summary: Zero-shot story visualization depicts textual narratives as image sequences without pre-existing text-image training pairs.
The work targets automated multi-character visualization and the limitations of manual portrait initialization and poor interaction quality.
LeMon automates portrait initialization through LLM-based matching and refines portraits with a graph-based diffusion model.
The authors report higher-quality visualizations than existing approaches across varied multi-character stories.

source_observation.claim: The framework combines external character resources for initialization with iterative refinement based on modeled character interactions.

interpretation.claim: Separating initial identity grounding from interaction-aware refinement may help maintain character distinctness and compatibility in sequential generation.

application.claim: A related visualization system could use retrieved exemplars for initial entity grounding, followed by graph-based iterative refinement for consistency across interacting entities.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this strategy generalizes beyond the reported story-visualization setting or how much manual intervention remains in practice.

unknowns: No datasets, evaluation metrics, quantitative results, or baseline details are provided.
The abstract does not specify the diffusion architecture, graph construction procedure, or portrait-refinement algorithm.
The abstract does not report limitations, failure cases, or reproducibility details beyond code availability.
